## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Dutiyasuṇisāvimānavatthu* ("Second Daughter-in-Law Mansion", Vv 14) is a canonical verse text belonging to the *Vimānavatthu* in the Pali Tipiṭaka [SuttaCentral]. The text recounts how a celestial being (*deva*) explains to an interlocutor the past wholesome action that led to her sublime heavenly rebirth: having offered a honey-covered cake during her human life, she attained rebirth in a celestial mansion and the delight of Nandana Park [SuttaCentral]. SuttaCentral lists five modern translations of the text across five languages [SuttaCentral].
No cross-language parallels meeting the threshold score of 10 are recorded by DharmaNexus, and SuttaCentral lists no direct external parallels [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. However, DharmaNexus detects extensive internal text reuse across the Pali canon, recording 214 matches across 36 other Pali texts [DharmaNexus]. Its verses share near-total correspondence with the preceding companion text, the *Paṭhamasuṇisāvimānavatthu* (Vv 13, §0.1–9.1 with 0.95 similarity), as well as formulaic descriptions shared with numerous other *Vimānavatthu* poems, including the *Guttilavimānavatthu* (Vv 33), *Tiladakkhiṇavimānavatthu* (Vv 10), *Dīpavimānavatthu* (Vv 9), and *Dutiyanāvāvimānavatthu* (Vv 7) [DharmaNexus]. Substantial segments (§1.1–9.1) are also preserved and expounded in the commentary, the *Vimānavatthu-aṭṭhakathā*, with additional reuse found in the *Petavatthu-aṭṭhakathā* [DharmaNexus].
